what_happened: Task 532's described defect (roadmap-integration.sh --regenerate silently aborting against a Stage-based ROADMAP.md) is the exact same issue already fully fixed by task 371 (completed 2026-10-10, archived at specs/archive/371_roadmap_generator_stage_layout_and_silent_abort/), including the stage-layout round-trip, the permanent loud destructive-overwrite refusal, and the always-present stderr marker. Live re-verification today against this repo's actual specs/ROADMAP.md and a synthetic unknown-layout fixture confirms both code paths work exactly as task 371's summary describes: --regenerate --dry-run on the real classic-layout ROADMAP.md exits 0 with a minimal, state-accurate diff; against an unrecognized layout it exits 1 with a named ERROR: line and no write. The one follow-up bug task 371 recorded (prune_next_body() CLI-flag-parsing) was also already fixed by task 388. No implementation work remains; research recommends closing task 532 as covered-by-closed (371) rather than dispatching a plan/implement phase.

Four of five carried figures in the task description re-verified as STALE (the silent-abort premise, the Stage-layout claim, the marker counts, and the coverage-appendix-only claim); the research report's own '68/68 tests' figure is also stale at 93/93 today. Only the narrowest claim -- the success path emitting no named diagnostic -- still reproduces, and the research report had recommended closing without testing it. Plan scoped to that residual gap only.

Running --regenerate twice against a scratch copy and diffing the two runs' own output (rather than only the file) exposed that a changed write and a no-op write are byte-identical in exit code, stdout, and stderr marker. That single two-run comparison is what distinguished 'close as covered-by-closed' from 'a narrow real defect remains', and it was corroborated independently by roadmap-update.md already promising the distinguishability the script does not deliver.

Batch Gate Deferral directive applied cleanly: scoped discharge via 'run-all.sh --only test-roadmap-generation.sh' (105/105 pass) and 'verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 22' (shellcheck) substituted for the independent full gate sweep. The full sweep was still attempted once for visibility and showed unrelated flakiness (gate8/gate10 timeouts under concurrent-sibling load); re-running gate10's underlying check (validate-state.sh --deep) in isolation passed in 61s, confirming the timeout was resource contention, not a regression.

Full 'verify-deploy.sh' sweep (run outside the scoped discharge, for visibility only) reports a pre-existing, out-of-file_scope Gate 20 context-budget overage (orchestrate.md/SKILL.md eager-load 71712B vs baseline 70400B) and a deployed-tree drift in context/formats/frontmatter.md (trailing newline only). Neither file is in this task's file_scope or touched by any commit this dispatch made; git status/log confirm both are pre-existing and unrelated. This task's own four files are confirmed byte-identical between source store and deployed tree.
